newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt fund managers boost durations - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt fund managers boost durations - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers boosted durations over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

"Durations rebounded after four straight down weeks, and are now at 105.8 percent (as a percentage of benchmark) ... on a dollar-weighted basis," explained MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
That represents a rise from 105.4 percent in the week ended October 7.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 14 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 20 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 34 percent, up from 26 percent in the week ended October 7.
Fifty-two percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 54 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.68 percent, against 2.89 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 20 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 21 percent in the previous week, while 26 percent underweighted it. The remaining 54 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 43 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 18 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
